question: If the front tire goes flat while riding, how will the motorcycle typically handle?
choice_a: The steering will feel "heavy," making it particularly hazardous to keep balance
choice_b: The rear of the motorcycle will jerk or sway from side to side
choice_c: There will be no noticeable change in handling
explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. If the front tire goes flat, the steering will feel heavy, which is particularly hazardous because it affects your steering and you have to steer well to keep your balance.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.28, 'Tire Failure'

question: If either tire goes flat while riding, what should a rider do?
choice_b: Hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, keep a straight course, and edge to the side of the road to stop
choice_c: Accelerate to a safe area before slowing
explanation: If either tire goes flat: hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep a straight course; if braking is required, gradually apply the brake of the tire that isn't flat, and when the motorcycle slows, edge to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.29, 'Tire Failure'

question: If the throttle sticks and twisting it back and forth doesn't free it, what should a rider do?
choice_a: Apply the rear brake only, with the throttle still open
choice_b: Continue riding normally and address it after the trip
choice_c: Immediately operate the engine cut-off switch and squeeze the clutch lever at the same time
choice_d: Turn off the headlight to conserve the electrical system
explanation: If the situation allows, twist the throttle back and forth to try to free it. If it stays stuck, immediately operate the engine cut-off switch and squeeze the clutch lever at the same time to remove power from the rear wheel, then move to a safe area and stop.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.29, 'Stuck Throttle'

question: What is a "wobble" as described in the manual?
choice_a: A sound the engine makes when low on oil
choice_b: A slow, gentle drift to one side of the lane
choice_c: A normal vibration that occurs only above 70 mph
choice_d: When the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed
explanation: A wobble occurs when the front wheel and handlebars suddenly start to shake from side to side at any speed. Most wobbles can be traced to improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.29-30, 'Wobble'

question: If a wobble starts, what should a rider do?
choice_a: Grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, close the throttle gradually, and move weight forward and down
choice_b: Try to accelerate out of the wobble
choice_c: Apply the brakes hard to stop the shaking
choice_d: Let go of the handlebars to let the motorcycle correct itself
explanation: Trying to accelerate out of a wobble will only make the motorcycle more unstable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly but don't fight the wobble, close the throttle gradually (do not apply the brakes, which could make the wobble worse), and move your weight as far forward and down as possible.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.30, 'Wobble'

question: If the drive chain or belt breaks while riding, what will a rider notice?
choice_a: A sudden surge of extra power
choice_b: An instant loss of power to the rear wheel
choice_c: No noticeable change until the next stop
choice_d: The front wheel will lock immediately
explanation: If the chain or belt breaks, you'll notice an instant loss of power to the rear wheel. Close the throttle and brake to a stop in a safe area.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.30, 'Drive Train Problems'

question: What is a common first sign that a motorcycle's engine is about to seize?
choice_a: The headlight flickers on and off
choice_c: A loss of engine power or a change in the engine's sound, usually caused by low oil
explanation: When the engine locks or freezes it is usually low on oil, and the first sign may be a loss of engine power or a change in the engine's sound; squeeze the clutch to disengage the engine, pull off the road and stop, and check the oil.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.30, 'Engine Seizure'

question: If you are being chased by a dog while riding, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Swerve sharply back and forth to confuse the animal
choice_b: Kick at the animal to drive it away
choice_c: Stop completely and wait for the animal to leave
choice_d: Downshift, approach slowly, then accelerate and leave the animal behind
explanation: Motorcycles seem to attract dogs. If you are being chased, downshift and approach the animal slowly, then as you approach, accelerate and leave the animal behind -- don't kick at it, and keep control of your motorcycle.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.30-31, 'Animals'

question: For larger animals such as deer, elk, or cattle in the roadway, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Brake and prepare to stop, since they are unpredictable
choice_c: Sound the horn continuously and maintain speed
explanation: For larger animals (deer, elk, cattle), brake and prepare to stop -- they are unpredictable.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.31, 'Animals'

question: If in traffic and a small animal darts into your path, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Always swerve out of your lane no matter the traffic
choice_b: Remain in your lane -- hitting something small is less dangerous than hitting something big, like a car
choice_c: Brake as hard as possible regardless of surrounding traffic
choice_d: Come to a complete stop in your lane
explanation: You should do everything you safely can to avoid hitting an animal, but if you are in traffic, remain in your lane -- hitting something small is less dangerous to you than hitting something big, like a car.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.30, 'Animals'

question: If an insect or pebble strikes a rider's face protection and smears or cracks it, what should the rider do?
choice_a: Close the eyes briefly until the impact passes
choice_b: Immediately remove the face protection while still riding
choice_c: Keep eyes on the road and hands on the handlebars, then pull off the road when safe to repair the damage
choice_d: Swerve to shake off the debris
explanation: If face protection gets smeared or cracked by a flying object, it might be difficult to see. Whatever happens, keep your eyes on the road and hands on the handlebars, and pull off the road to repair the damage when safe.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.31, 'Flying Objects'

question: Before pulling off the road onto the roadside to rest or check the motorcycle, what should a rider check?
choice_a: Whether other riders are already stopped in the exact same spot
choice_b: Only whether there is a nearby gas station
choice_c: Nothing -- any roadside surface is safe to ride onto
choice_d: Whether the roadside surface is firm enough to ride on, slowing down if it's soft grass, loose sand, or uncertain
explanation: Check the roadside to make sure the surface is firm enough to ride on; if it's soft grass, loose sand, or you're just not sure, slow way down before you turn onto it.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.31, 'Getting Off the Road'

question: When pulling off the road, why should a rider signal and check mirrors and do a head check before taking any action?
choice_a: Drivers behind might not expect the rider to slow down and change direction
choice_b: It is only a courtesy with no safety benefit
choice_c: State law only requires this on divided highways
choice_d: It is unnecessary if the shoulder is clearly visible
explanation: Signal, since drivers behind might not expect you to slow down and change direction -- check your mirror and make a head check before you take any action, then pull off the road as far as you can.
source_note: MN DPS Motorcycle and Motorized Bicycle Manual (PS30001-21, 11/2021), p.31, 'Getting Off the Road'
